# Seaborn vs Matplotlib

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import seaborn as sns

print("=== Matplotlib vs Seaborn ===\n")

# Create data
np.random.seed(42)
data = np.random.normal(0, 1, (100, 3))
df = pd.DataFrame(data, columns=['A', 'B', 'C'])

# Add categorical data
df['Category'] = np.random.choice(['X', 'Y', 'Z'], 100)

print("=== Matplotlib: Basic Histogram ===\n")

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.hist(df['A'], bins=20, color='blue', alpha=0.7)
plt.title('Matplotlib Histogram')
plt.xlabel('Value')
plt.ylabel('Frequency')
plt.show()

print("\n=== Seaborn: Enhanced Histogram ===\n")

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.histplot(df['A'], bins=20, kde=True, color='blue')
plt.title('Seaborn Histogram with KDE')
plt.xlabel('Value')
plt.ylabel('Frequency')
plt.show()

print("\n=== Matplotlib: Scatter Plot ===\n")

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.scatter(df['A'], df['B'], alpha=0.6)
plt.title('Matplotlib Scatter Plot')
plt.xlabel('A')
plt.ylabel('B')
plt.show()

print("\n=== Seaborn: Enhanced Scatter ===\n")

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.scatterplot(data=df, x='A', y='B', hue='Category', style='Category')
plt.title('Seaborn Scatter with Hue and Style')
plt.show()

print("\n=== Matplotlib: Box Plot ===\n")

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.boxplot([df['A'], df['B'], df['C']], labels=['A', 'B', 'C'])
plt.title('Matplotlib Box Plot')
plt.ylabel('Value')
plt.show()

print("\n=== Seaborn: Enhanced Box Plot ===\n")

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.boxplot(data=df[['A', 'B', 'C']])
plt.title('Seaborn Box Plot')
plt.ylabel('Value')
plt.show()

print("\n=== Seaborn: Pair Plot ===\n")

# Pair plot shows all relationships
sns.pairplot(df[['A', 'B', 'C']])
plt.suptitle('Seaborn Pair Plot', y=1.02)
plt.show()

print("\n=== Seaborn: Heatmap ===\n")

# Correlation heatmap
corr = df[['A', 'B', 'C']].corr()
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 6))
sns.heatmap(corr, annot=True, cmap='coolwarm', center=0)
plt.title('Seaborn Correlation Heatmap')
plt.show()

print("\n=== When to use which? ===\n")

print("Matplotlib:")
print("  ✅ Full control over every detail")
print("  ✅ Lightweight")
print("  ✅ Works everywhere")
print("  ✅ Good for simple plots")

print("\nSeaborn:")
print("  ✅ Beautiful default styles")
print("  ✅ Built-in statistical plots")
print("  ✅ Easy to use")
print("  ✅ Great for exploring data")
print("  ✅ Integrates with Pandas")

phase1.explanation:
🐍 **Seaborn builds on Matplotlib for statistical visualization.**

**Comparison:**
| Feature | Matplotlib | Seaborn |
|---------|------------|---------|
| Control | Maximum | Less |
| Default style | Basic | Beautiful |
| Statistical plots | Manual | Built-in |
| Pandas integration | Manual | Native |
| Learning curve | Steep | Gentle |

**Seaborn plot types:**
```python
# Distribution
sns.histplot(data, kde=True)
sns.kdeplot(data)
sns.rugplot(data)

# Categorical
sns.barplot(data, x='cat', y='value')
sns.boxplot(data, x='cat', y='value')
sns.violinplot(data, x='cat', y='value')

# Relationships
sns.scatterplot(data, x='a', y='b')
sns.lineplot(data, x='a', y='b')
sns.pairplot(data)

# Matrix
sns.heatmap(correlation_matrix)
sns.clustermap(matrix)
```

phase2.explanation:
**Seaborn expects specific data formats!**

**What's wrong:**
1. Seaborn works best with DataFrames
2. Numpy arrays don't have column names
3. Results in unlabeled plots

**The fix:**
```python
import seaborn as sns
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Method 1: Use DataFrame with named columns
data = pd.DataFrame({
    'A': np.random.normal(0, 1, 100),
    'B': np.random.normal(0, 1, 100),
    'C': np.random.normal(0, 1, 100)
})

# This works!
sns.boxplot(data=data)

# Method 2: Use long format
df_long = pd.melt(data)
sns.boxplot(data=df_long, x='variable', y='value')

# Method 3: Specify columns
sns.boxplot(data=data, x='A', y='B')
```

**Python-chan says:**
"Seaborn works best with Pandas DataFrames. Use named columns for clean plots."
